newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ, Australia to examine investment agreement.
newsitem.headline: NZ, Australia to examine investment agreement.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Wednesday he had agreed with Australian Treasurer Peter Costello to examine the possibility of a trans-Tasman agreement on investment.

"A trans-Tasman agreement on investment could provide greater certainty, and officials should examine this issue anew, consistent with international obligations relating to investment flows," Birch said in a statement.
Birch said the double taxation agrement between the two countries, last renegotiated in 1994, removed a number of tax barriers to an efficient trans-Tasman investment market.

"But it does not address the important issues arising from the double taxation of dividends where companies resident on one side of the Tasman are taxed on income earned through subsidiaries resident on the other side," he said.

Birch said such income was subject to both Australian and New Zealand tax when distributed to the ultimate shareholder. In contrast, if the dividend were from a domestic company on domestic-sourced income, it would face only one layer of tax.

Officials would work together over the next six months to examine tax changes to prevent loss of imputation credits in such cases, Birch said. They would look at revenue, tax base and implementation issues, as well as compliance and administration.

Birch released a copy of a letter to Costello in which he wrote: "We will...aim to avoid to the fullest possible extent further restrictions on investors and confirm that trans-Tasman investment should be subject to minimum constraint both now and in the future."

He said he and Costello would write to the Australian Foreign Investment Review Board and the New Zealand Overseas Investment Commission stressing the need to maintain liberal administration procedures and asking them to identify ways of streamlining these in order to cut compliance costs.
Birch said he and Costello had agreed at this stage only to examine the issues, rather than on specific changes.
Costello replied in a letter that he looked forward to seeing progress in the coming months on the issues raised.
Birch's announcement came on the eve of the annual conference of the Australia-New Zealand Business Council in Auckland. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
